clue.text: I can't remember names CIA put out

indicators.note: put out suggests something disturbed or disarranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone forgets the names of the agents the CIA has released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges NAMES and CIA together. The definition is a first-person description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering memory loss could say of themselves that they cannot recall things.

clue.text: Oppose dance, then go along

parts.note: to play a team is to oppose it in a match
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a dance and then agrees to come anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for cooperating with others means agreeing to their plans rather than resisting.

clue.text: He wrote 'Oliver!', fine composer

parts.note: Lionel Bart wrote the stage musical Oliver!
fine means OK, all right

explanation.surface: Praise for the writer of the musical Oliver! as a fine composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Talk at length about GI's cryptic puzzle

indicators.note: about means the talk goes round the other letters

parts.note: to jaw is to chatter on at length

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the letters of GI's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone talks endlessly about a soldier's crossword puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk at length' sounds like a description of someone chatting, but it is a verb meaning to jaw; 'cryptic' and 'about' do the work on GI's.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces to reassemble is a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Student paid to get knowledge

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
earning means being paid for work

explanation.surface: A student is paid to acquire knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly erudition acquired by study is a synonym for knowledge.

clue.text: Scottish dramatist in Welsh port, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the port's name is said aloud

parts.note: Barry is a port town in south Wales

explanation.surface: A Scottish playwright turns up in a Welsh harbour town, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie, author of Peter Pan, was a Scottish playwright.

clue.text: Dahl book one lad tossed on rug

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the rug

parts.note: a mat is a small rug
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A Roald Dahl book flung onto a rug by a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the shuffled one-and-lad after the rug, the reverse of how it reads on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Matilda is a 1988 children's novel by Roald Dahl.

clue.text: Scotch broth? Pound

indicators.note: to scotch is to wreck or put an end to, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Scotch broth is priced at a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like part of the soup's name but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound and to beat rhythmically are synonyms, as a heart does.

clue.text: Ring with right answer for 'fabled monster'

parts.note: to chime is to ring

explanation.surface: A quiz: ring the bell with the correct answer for 'fabled monster'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing beast, part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Played fairly, winning — make a big profit?

parts.note: to play clean is to play fairly
up means ahead or winning

explanation.surface: A player who played fairly and won made a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for making a large gain means profiting handsomely.

clue.text: Forward almost missing header

indicators.note: missing its header means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A football forward almost misses with a header.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward, header and missing all suggest football.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward and premature both mean ahead of the usual time, as in a forward spring.

clue.text: Club official, more confident following adjustment of rate

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first
adjustment means changing, so the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more confident

explanation.surface: A club official is more sure of things once the rate is adjusted.
explanation.definitionFit: A club's finances are managed by the officer who keeps its accounts.

clue.text: Popular chess opponents? On paper

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the two sides in chess are black and white

explanation.surface: A question whether two chess opponents are well liked, on paper at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Something written down in ink on a page is set out in print, on paper.

clue.text: Advanced fortune to make a musical

parts.note: came means approached or advanced
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Someone advanced a fortune to stage a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is a Lerner and Loewe stage musical about King Arthur's court.

clue.text: Fail to catch service, according to drunkard in muddle?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs s sounds into sh sounds, so the phrase is pronounced that way

parts.note: to miss is to fail to catch; mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A drunk misses church and ends up in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk saying 'miss mass' slurs both S sounds into SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumbled hotchpotch of things is a confused mess, a muddle.

clue.text: Enormous film

definitions.meaning: huge, on the scale of the Titans

explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, and is also the title of a famous film about the ship.

clue.text: Model Spanish kingdom once after power

indicators.note: after means the kingdom comes after the power

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
Aragon was a medieval kingdom in Spain

explanation.surface: A model historic Spanish kingdom following a seizure of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of a quality.

clue.text: Domestic residence? Yes, in the States

definitions.text: Domestic residence? Yes, in the States

parts.note: a domestic is a family quarrel, a row
a house is a residence

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is a home and answering that it is, in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like an adjective for the residence but is a noun, a household row. 'Yes, in the States' confirms the term is American, for a terraced house.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage it is one of a terrace of joined houses, a domestic dwelling.

clue.text: He, Tarzan, shot in Israeli town

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tarzan is shot in an Israeli town.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth is a town in northern Israel, known as Jesus's childhood home.

clue.text: The dance to give one pause for thought?

definitions.text: The dance to give one pause for thought?

parts.words: The dance to give one pause for thought?
parts.note: a dance whose name suggests a pause, as a hesitation is a pause

explanation.definitionFit: The hesitation waltz is a ballroom dance with steps where the dancers pause.

clue.text: Jazz musician, that woman's husband?

parts.note: her means belonging to that woman
man can mean husband, as in man and wife

explanation.surface: A question whether the jazz musician is that woman's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Herman was an American jazz clarinettist and bandleader.

clue.text: Host runs wearing skimpy article of beachwear

indicators.note: wearing means the beachwear is around the runs

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy bikini bottom
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A host goes jogging wearing a tiny swimsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great crowd or multitude, like a dense mass of people.

clue.text: Sharp, tiny chap in unit

indicators.note: in means the chap is put inside the unit

parts.note: one is a unit
Tiny Tim is the boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A small man in a military unit is keen.
explanation.walkthrough: Sharp, as in 'at six o'clock sharp', means punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp after a time means exactly punctual, arriving at the stated hour.

clue.text: Queue to get on river vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the queue sits above the river

parts.note: a line is a queue

explanation.surface: Queueing to get on a river boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: In new term, admit particular type, painter

indicators.note: admit means the rearranged term takes in the other piece
new means remade, so the letters of term are rearranged

parts.note: a brand is a particular type or make

explanation.surface: In the new school term, admitting a particular kind of painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TERM into REMT, which 'admit' opens to take in BRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great Dutch Golden Age painter.

clue.text: Proprietor in state of depression having day off

indicators.note: off means the day is taken away

parts.note: a downer is a depressed mood

explanation.surface: A shop proprietor feeling low takes a day off.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who owns a business or property.

clue.text: As is nacre, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests unexpected change, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is like mother-of-pearl, surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word but is the definition: As is the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of the poisonous element number 33.

clue.text: Creature in rolling vessel in dangerous frenzy

indicators.note: in means the vessel goes inside the frenzy

parts.note: must is the dangerous frenzied state of a male elephant

indicators.note: rolling means turning over, so the vessel is read backwards

parts.note: an ark is a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: An animal in a rolling ship is in a dangerous frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: Must (also spelt musth) is the frenzied state of a bull elephant in season; 'rolling' turns the vessel over before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A muskrat is a large aquatic North American rodent, a creature.
